I started using a smart lock on my front door about five or six years ago, and I've tried quite a few models along the way. For most users, the ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint is a solid option — it supports Apple Home, has built-in Wi-Fi, and offers a comprehensive set of unlock methods. Whether you prefer using your fingerprint or a simple PIN code, it pretty much has you covered.

HomeKit Weekly is a series dedicated to smart home accessories, automation tips, and everything related to Apple's smart home framework.

Apple Home support, but no Home Key

ULTRALOQ positions the Bolt Fingerprint as its first smart lock with full Apple Home integration, and it's precisely this integration that drew me in. Honestly, I still miss Touch ID on my iPhone. You can lock or unlock the door through the Home app or Siri, and if you have a HomePod or Apple TV acting as a home hub, the experience is just like any other Apple Home accessory — you can include it in automation scenes, control it remotely, and it's fully compatible with various scenes and automation workflows.

However, for me, there's always been one missing feature: Home Key. Being able to simply tap your iPhone or Apple Watch to open the door is what truly feels like an upgrade. Even though this is the only thing missing, it's not exactly a deal-breaker.

I hope ULTRALOQ will consider adding this feature in their next model, because with Home Key included, this lock could go from "good" to "near perfect." At the same time, the lock also supports Amazon Alexa, Google Home, SmartThings, and IFTTT — so regardless of which smart home platform you prefer, or even if you want to switch platforms down the road, it offers excellent flexibility. It uses 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi rather than Bluetooth, meaning you can perform basic remote control through its app without needing an additional bridge.

Unlock methods galore

The Bolt Fingerprint offers an impressive array of unlock methods. The fingerprint reader can store up to 50 fingerprints and 50 passcodes, you can unlock it via the mobile app, have it auto-unlock as you approach the door, or use voice control through Siri, Alexa, or Google Assistant. It also comes with two physical keys, so even if the battery dies, you won't be completely locked out. For me, a smart lock without a physical key as a backup is simply unacceptable.

You can also set up to 50 custom passcodes and distribute one-time or time-limited codes to friends, visitors, or cleaning staff. If you have a rental property, this feature alone is worth the price of admission.

There's also a "Lockout Mode" that temporarily disables all electronic unlock methods, including passcodes and app unlocking, providing extra peace of mind for those on extended trips, making the home more secure when left vacant. Personally, I don't consider these features essential for a smart lock, but having them certainly doesn't hurt.

Installation and adding to Apple Home

Over the past few years, I've installed more smart locks than I can count, so I've gotten quite experienced by now. As long as I have the right tools, I can usually get it done in about ten minutes. Assuming you're replacing an existing modern deadbolt, the installation process doesn't require any wiring or drilling holes in the wall. A Phillips screwdriver is all you need, and remember to replace the strike plate on the door frame as well.

After adding the lock to your Apple Home setup and assigning it to a room, you can control it through the Home app or incorporate it into automations and scenes — triggering multiple actions at once, such as having the lights turn on immediately when the front door is unlocked.

ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint overall review

Overall, if you don't need Home Key support, the ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint is a reliable choice. Fingerprint unlocking will most likely become your everyday go-to method. The installation process is also very straightforward. I'm currently using this lock on my office door because there are always laptops sitting around waiting to be shipped out, and I want an extra layer of security. The auto-unlock feature when approaching the door is genuinely excellent, and you can see at any time who has come and gone. Fingerprint unlocking gives me the same feeling I had when I used Touch ID.

You can purchase the Bolt Fingerprint directly from Amazon or the ULTRALOQ official website.
